_rotation_note: The daily job picks the next business each morning - rotating among ward businesses with priority to spotlight requests from owners and newly opened spots. Keep yesterday's entries in history.

current.name: Smyth + The Loyalist
current.blurb: Two restaurants in one: the two-Michelin-star Smyth upstairs, and downstairs The Loyalist, home to what many call Chicago's best burger.

history.name: Lou Mitchell's
history.blurb: A Chicago breakfast landmark at the original starting line of Route 66, serving since 1923. Lou Mitchell's is famous for double-yolk eggs, fluffy skillet omelettes served in the pan, and the free Milk Duds and donut holes handed out while you wait for a table.

history.name: Green Street Smoked Meats
history.blurb: Tucked down an alley off Green Street, this rollicking barbecue joint serves Texas-style brisket, ribs, and burnt ends by the pound on butcher paper. Cold beer, picnic tables, and a lively bar make it a West Loop staple.

history.name: Monteverde Restaurant & Pastificio
history.blurb: Chef Sarah Grueneberg, a James Beard Award winner, turns out some of the country's most celebrated handmade pasta from an open pastificio counter on Madison Street. The cacio whey pepe and the ragu alla napoletana are neighborhood legends, and the bar pours a deep Italian wine list.

history.name: Mario's Italian Lemonade
history.blurb: A Taylor Street summer institution since 1954, Mario's is the little red-and-green stand where Chicagoans line up for hand-shaved Italian lemonade in flavors from lemon and cantaloupe to peach and watermelon. Cash only, open only in the warm months, and worth every minute of the wait.

history.name: Sepia
history.blurb: Set in a restored 1890s print shop, this Michelin-starred West Loop mainstay pairs refined American cooking with a warm, timeless room. It has been a special-occasion favorite in the neighborhood for well over a decade.

history.name: The Publican
history.blurb: A beer-hall-style anchor of Fulton Market, The Publican built its name on oysters, house charcuterie, and pork served at long communal tables. It helped put the neighborhood on the map as a dining destination.

history.name: The Original Pancake House
history.blurb: A breakfast institution since 1953, famous for the oven-baked Dutch Baby and apple pancakes. The West Loop location on Madison fills its striped-awning patio all summer long.

history.name: Lou Mitchell's
history.blurb: A Chicago breakfast landmark at the original starting line of Route 66, serving since 1923. Lou Mitchell's is famous for double-yolk eggs, skillet omelettes served in the pan, and the free Milk Duds and donut holes handed out while you wait.

history.name: Au Cheval
history.blurb: The dark, clubby diner behind what many call the best cheeseburger in America. The wait on Randolph Street is legendary, the bologna sandwich and the eggs are worth it, and the whole room hums well past midnight.

history.name: Girl & the Goat
history.blurb: Chef Stephanie Izard's flagship put Randolph Street's Restaurant Row on the national map. The wood-fired, globally-spiced small plates, from the famous goat empanadas to the pan-fried shishito peppers, still pack the room nightly.

history.name: Bavette's Bar & Boeuf
history.address: 218 W. Kinzie St, River North edge
history.blurb: A candlelit, 1920s-style steakhouse just north of the ward with a jazz soundtrack and deep leather booths. The dry-aged steaks, roasted bone marrow, and towering chocolate cake keep it perennially hard to book.

history.name: Formento's
history.blurb: A love letter to Italian-American red-sauce classics on Restaurant Row. Sunday gravy, house pastas, and a chicken Parm that regulars swear by, all in a handsome, old-school room.

history.name: El Che Steakhouse & Bar
history.blurb: An Argentine-inspired steakhouse where nearly everything touches the open hearth. The wood-fired grill, empanadas, and Malbec-heavy list make it one of the West Loop's most distinctive rooms.

history.name: Bar Siena
history.blurb: A bustling Randolph Street trattoria known for wood-fired pizzas, house pastas, and a lively bar. Its patio is one of Restaurant Row's favorite warm-weather perches.

history.name: Gibsons Italia
history.address: 233 N. Canal St, Fulton River District
history.blurb: The Italian-leaning riverside sibling of the classic Chicago steakhouse, with sweeping views of the Chicago River. Prime steaks, fresh pasta, and a see-and-be-seen patio.

history.name: J.P. Graziano Grocery
history.blurb: A century-old Italian importer and sandwich counter on Randolph Street. The Mr. G, a stacked Italian sub with sharp provolone and hot giardiniera, has a devoted citywide following.

history.name: Publican Quality Meats
history.blurb: The butcher shop, bakery, and sandwich cafe next to The Publican. Grab a pastrami or porchetta sandwich, a loaf of bread, and house-cured meats to take home.

history.name: Swift & Sons
history.blurb: A grand, brass-and-leather steakhouse in a former cold-storage building, anchoring the Fulton Market dining scene. Dry-aged steaks, a raw bar, and a soaring room built for a night out.

history.name: RM Champagne Salon
history.blurb: A hidden, cobblestone-courtyard Champagne bar off Green Street, romantic and candlelit, pouring bubbles and French-leaning small plates. One of the West Loop's most charming date spots.

history.name: H Mart West Loop
history.blurb: The beloved Korean-American grocery chain's downtown Chicago store, stocking fresh produce, seafood, kimchi, and hard-to-find pantry staples from across Asia. The food hall upstairs draws a lunch crowd from all over the Loop.

history.name: Open Books West Loop
history.blurb: A nonprofit used bookstore where every purchase funds literacy programs for Chicago students. Tens of thousands of donated titles line the shelves, and volunteers keep the mission running.

history.name: CrossTown Fitness
history.blurb: A locally owned gym on Madison Street known for high-energy group classes, personal training, and a neighborhood feel that big chains cannot match. A West Loop fixture for over a decade.

history.name: Madison Street Books
history.blurb: The West Loop's independent bookstore, with a thoughtfully curated selection, a resident shop dog, and a steady calendar of author events and book clubs. A cozy neighborhood anchor on Madison Street.

history.name: Capitol Hill Cleaners
history.blurb: A family-run dry cleaner that West Loop and Greektown neighbors have trusted for years with everything from suits to wedding dresses. Friendly counter service and quick turnarounds keep the regulars loyal.

history.name: Duck Duck Goat
history.blurb: Stephanie Izard's playful Chinese restaurant, with hand-pulled noodles, dim sum, and Peking duck in a bustling, mural-lined room.

history.name: Avec
history.blurb: One of Restaurant Row's originals, a warm cedar-lined room serving Mediterranean small plates from a wood oven at long communal tables. The chorizo-stuffed dates are a Chicago rite of passage.

history.name: Cruz Blanca Brewery & Taqueria
history.blurb: Rick Bayless's West Loop taqueria and brewery, pairing wood-grilled tacos and Oaxacan flavors with house-brewed beer and agave cocktails.

history.name: Rose Mary
history.blurb: Top Chef winner Joe Flamm's Adriatic cooking, a lively mash-up of Italian and Croatian, from handmade pastas to wood-grilled meats on Fulton Market.

history.name: The Aviary
history.blurb: The Alinea Group's avant-garde cocktail lounge, where drinks arrive as edible art and the menu of cocktails is unlike anywhere else in the city.

history.name: City Winery
history.blurb: An urban winery, restaurant, and intimate live-music venue on Randolph Street, making wine on site and hosting concerts on the riverfront patio.

history.name: Greek Islands
history.blurb: A Greektown institution since 1971, packed nightly for flaming saganaki, roast lamb, and warm hospitality across a big, bustling dining room.

history.name: Athena Greek Restaurant
history.blurb: A Greektown mainstay known for classic taverna cooking and one of the neighborhood's largest garden patios, framed by Parthenon-style columns.

history.name: Roister
history.blurb: The Alinea Group's rowdy, open-kitchen restaurant, famous for its whole fried chicken and a counter that puts you right in the fire.
